description:
src/lib.rs:213-285 (test_support::MockBackend) uses std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<...>> guarding the test state and locks it inside async fns (account_exists, get_objects, destroy_object, calendar_has_events).

Currently every such call site drops the guard before any .await — there are no .await calls between the .lock() and the implicit Drop. So the code is correct today. But this is a fragile pattern: any future contributor adding 'an await for some reason' (e.g. asynchronously serializing one of the values inside the loop) will introduce a deadlock that clippy's await_holding_lock lint will catch only if explicitly enabled.

Three options, in order of robustness:
1. Switch to tokio::sync::Mutex (already a dep via the workspace tokio). Holds-across-await is fine and async-aware.
2. Keep std::sync::Mutex but enable #[deny(clippy::await_holding_lock)] at the test_support module level so the antipattern is caught at compile time.
3. Restructure to clone-out: 'let snapshot = self.state.lock().unwrap().clone();' then operate on the snapshot.

Option 2 is the cheapest. Option 1 is the most idiomatic for an async-only crate. Workspace already depends on tokio.

Severity P3 — test-only code, current behaviour correct, hazard is future-proofing.

Note: the same pattern applies to TrackingBackend in event.rs:953-1095 — Arc<Mutex<bool>> is fine but worth holding to the same standard.
notes:
Fixed in commit 6694e27 (option 2: deny lint at module level).

Applied to 10 sites across 7 server crates:
- jmap-{calendars,contacts,filenode,sharing,tasks}-server/src/lib.rs (cfg(test) test_support)
- jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs::tests::routing (TrackingBackend)
- jmap-{chat,filenode,mail,sharing}-server/tests/common/mod.rs (integration MemoryBackend)

Did NOT touch jmap-mail-server inline test_support — verified mail-server has no inline test_support module (its mock lives in tests/common/mod.rs only). chat-server src/lib.rs likewise has no inline test_support; its mock is in tests/common/mod.rs.

Per the bead's three options I picked option 2 (deny lint) because:
- Cheapest, no API churn
- Catches future hazard at compile time
- Module docs explain the hazard and point to tokio::sync::Mutex as the right fix if anyone needs to hold across .await
- No runtime perf or behavior change today

Gate: cargo build --workspace --all-targets, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace all green.
title: test_support::MockBackend uses std::sync::Mutex inside async fns — tokio::sync::Mutex would be safer
